earnings.title: McKESSON REPORTS FISCAL 2027 SECOND QUARTER RESULTS
highlights: Generated $3.1 billion of cash flow from operations and $2.9 billion of Free Cash Flow.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, McKesson generated cash from operations of $3.1 billion, and invested $123 million in capital expenditures, resulting in Free Cash Flow of $2.9 billion.

During the first six months of the fiscal year, McKesson generated cash from operations of $2.9 billion, and invested $275 million in capital expenditures, resulting in Free Cash Flow of $2.6 billion.

quotes.text: McKesson delivered another quarter of strong results, reflecting operational strength in our core business segments and disciplined execution across the enterprise.
quotes.by: Brian Tyler, chair and chief executive officer

quotes.text: The raise in fiscal 2027 Adjusted Earnings per Diluted Share guidance is underpinned by the strength in our business and the confidence we have in our ability to execute consistently.
quotes.by: Kenny Cheung, executive vice president and chief financial officer

outlook: Raised Adjusted Earnings per Diluted Share guidance range to $45.60 to $46.40, from the previous range of $44.20 to $45.00.
Fiscal 2027 Adjusted Earnings per Diluted Share guidance range indicates 17% to 19% growth compared to the prior year.
McKesson is raising its fiscal 2027 Adjusted Earnings per Diluted Share guidance to $45.60 to $46.40 from the previous range of $44.20 to $45.00.

items.heading: We experience costly and disruptive legal disputes.
We experience losses not covered by insurance or indemnification.
We experience costly legal disputes, government actions, and adverse publicity regarding our role in distributing controlled substances such as opioids.

We are subject to extensive, complex, challenging, and frequently changing healthcare, environmental, and other laws, and may experience increased costs to distribute controlled substances such as opioids.
We are subject to extensive and frequently changing laws relating to healthcare fraud, waste, and abuse.
We might lose our ability to purchase, store, or distribute pharmaceuticals, including controlled substances, and medical products.
